problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{\sqrt{61}} & \frac{6}{\sqrt{61}} \\ \frac{6}{\sqrt{61}} & \frac{5}{\sqrt{61}}\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{13} & 2 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]
$$

Find $|\text{det}(PQ)|$ given that $P$ is an orthogonal matrix.
worked_solution:
We use the following facts: 

- The determinant of a product is equal to the product of the determinants.

- The determinant of an orthogonal matrix $P$ is equal to $\pm 1.$

Applying these ideas, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\text{det}(PQ)| & =|\text{det}(P)\cdot \text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|(\pm 1)\cdot \text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|\pm 1|\cdot |\text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|\text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|\sqrt{13}\cdot \sqrt{5}-0\cdot 2| \\  & =\sqrt{65}\end{aligned}
$$
